newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO end Jericho talks without Hebron deal.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO end Jericho talks without Hebron deal.

text.p: Palestinian and Israeli negotiators failed in talks on Sunday in self-ruled Jericho to hammer out a deal on a delayed Israeli troop pullback from the West Bank town of Hebron, officials said.
"There is not a big change," Israeli chief negotiator Dan Shomron told reporters after the talks at the Palestinian Ministry of Local Government in autonomous Jericho.
The talks are stalemated over Israel's insistence that its troops be allowed to re-enter the 80 percent of Hebron slated to fall under PLO control if they are chasing suspected guerrillas.

"We hope the Israelis will stop putting obstacles in the path of progress. We hope they will not try to change anything in signed agreements, especially their demand to go freely in Palestinian areas," PLO negotiator Saeb Erekat told reporters.
PLO officials said the Jericho talks were "not serious" and did not say when negotiating teams would meet again. Shomron said it was possible to reach an agreement "soon".
The last bargaining round on Thursday, attended by U.S. diplomats, failed to bring the sides closer together.

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat has rejected any renegotiation of the Hebron accord, which was signed last year by a left-centre Israeli government ousted in May by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Netanyahu seeks to alter the Hebron deal to give more protection to some 400 militant Jewish settlers who live and study in heavily guarded enclaves among the more than 100,000 Palestinians of the town.
Under the interim PLO-Israel peace deal, Hebron was to be handed over to Palestinian self-rule last year, but Israel delayed the transfer for security reasons.

Erekat said Palestinian and Israeli teams were preparing letters of assurance to be exchanged between Arafat and Netanyahu. He said Palestinians wanted guarantees of continued implementation of peace deals made earlier with Israel.

"We submitted a list of issues we want mentioned in the letter, which include specifying dates for resumption of final status talks, dates for talks on implementing interim outstanding issues which require further negotiations and dates for implementing issues that don't require further negotiation."

Israeli spokesman Moshe Fogel said of the letter Israel wants from the Palestinians: "The principle of reciprocity is a point we believe is an integral part of the agreements, and we want Palestinians to live up to the agreements".

"Prime Minister Netanyahu said many times he was willing to live up to the agreements, but there are a series of Palestinian violations of the agreement and a number of issues that Palestinians have to address," Fogel told Reuters.
